sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Lichdragon Fortissax** is a boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Fortissax is an Ancient Dragon who was once known as the "mightiest boulderstone", known for its use of twin red lightning stakes, and the sibling of Ancient Dragon Lansseax.

During the Age of the Erdtree, the Ancient Dragons warred against the forces of Leyndell, after an assault on the royal capital by the great Ancient Dragon Gransax. Fortissax was challenged by Godwyn the Golden, who fought to the last. Godwyn defeated Fortissax, but he befriended his fallen foe, and their bond gave rise to the Ancient Dragon Cult of the Royal Capital. Through this friendship, Godwyn gained the ability to wield golden lightning, while the dragons gained acceptance as part of the Golden Order.

On the Night of Black Knives, Godwyn was slain by assassins. Godwyn would die in soul alone, with his body condemned to undeath, as it mutated beyond recognition. Fortissax fought long and hard against the death within its companion, becoming corrupted by death in the process. The Lichdragon is encountered within the Deathbed Dream after securing the Cursemark of Death and giving it to Fia, another companion of Godwyn's. Following Fortissax's defeat, Fia gestates the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince, which may usher in an age of death restored.

As well as being able to breathe fire like other Ancient Dragons, Fortissax possesses the ability to summon a storm of gold and black lightning bolts which cover a wide area and inflict Death Blight. It can also summon a bolt of red lightning, which it slams into the ground, releasing waves of red lightning in multiple directions. After its health has been reduced to 60%, it gains the ability to summon two lightning spears at once, as well as a divebomb ability which is followed by a spinning attack using a lightning glaive.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Lightning Strike** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- **Guaranteed Drop:** Weeping Peninsula
- Lightning Strike is received upon defeating the Scarab at the bottom of the ravine splitting the Weeping Peninsula region in half. The stone platforms on either side of this can be used to descend safely. Note that it's surrounded by large bats and that lightning strikes constantly hit around this area.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown: Creates an uneven line of lightning strikes with Lightning Attack Power equal to 246% of Incantation Scaling per hit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Casting the spell costs 32 points of Stamina.
- Deals 5 Stance damage per hit.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- If the incantation hits a watery surface or an enemy standing on such a surface, a small area of effect attack with Lightning Attack Power equal to 50% of Incantation Scaling will be created that can hit the target foes and any adjacent enemies.
 - Also deals 2 Stance damage.
- Can hit multiple times per cast.
- Targeting may seem somewhat random due to the line that is being struck not being quite straight. However, the lightning bolts will always strike on the same intervals which means getting a feel for this and keeping a consistent distance will help with hitting greatly.
- This incantation does not work under low roofs.
 - This is because the targeting is done by sending a projectile straight above the caster's head that then travels forward while sending down lightning bolts periodically. This projectile is destroyed if it hits a solid object.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption.
 - This reduced the FP cost of casting from 21 to 19.
- Patch 1.04 decreased Stamina cost, increased cast speed and decreased recovery time.

sections.heading: See also
sections.markdown:

- Death Lightning, a Death Blight-inflicting version of this spell that is a spreading area of effect attack instead of a line

sections.markdown: Law of Causality** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Golden Order Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:

Can also be bought from the Twin Maiden Husks for 5,000 Runes after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown: Grants a unique Buff that lasts for 120 seconds. If the buffed target is damaged 5 times within 7 seconds, they explode, hitting for 487 Holy Attack Power against all enemies within a 4-meter radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast.
- Deals 7 Stance damage.
- Since the buff caster has to take damaging hits to trigger the effect, shields with 100% Guarded Damage Negation can prevent the effect from activating. Shields with almost but not quite 100% Guarded Damage Negation (such as the Lordsworn's Shield and its 94% Guarded Damage Negation against Physical damage) can minimize the damage needed.
- The final hit for the buffed can be triggered during a roll or another effect that reduces damage taken to 0. If this happens, the explosion's damage is also reduced to 0.
- Does not scale at all with Incantation Scaling, meaning its damage can only be increased with effects that can buff general damage, incantation damage, and Holy damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 extended effect time.
 - Duration was extended from 60 seconds to 120 seconds.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Law of Regression** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Golden Order Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for 10,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Golden Order Principia.
- Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then have that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
 - WARNING: Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving them the prayerbook then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character for the rest of that Journey.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown: Removes the Status Effects, Buffs, and debuffs from the caster and allies and enemies within a radius of 15 meters and also dispels all active spells within that effect radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 50 points of Stamina to cast.
- The requirements of the Sacred Seal don't need to be met to cast this spell, making it usable with no Faith investment.
- Surprisingly useful for crossing the Lake of Rot. While it's slower to cast than other spells and items, it's still somewhat useful for characters with high medium to high Intelligence but without the Faith needed for Flame, Cleanse Me or the materials for Preserving Boluses.
- Be careful when using it near allies so it doesn't remove their beneficial effects.
- Needed for Goldmask's quest: Reveals a secret referenced by Miriel when used while standing on top of the unknown artist's Wizened Finger message in front of the Radagon statue in Leyndell, Royal Capital, just outside of the Erdtree Sanctuary. Once you have revealed the secret message, you will be able to tell Goldmask about it to progress Brother Corhyn's quest.

- Costs 20 FP per cast.
- Costs 13 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- This spell reduces lightning damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where *LightningFortification* represents the effect magnitude:
 TotalLightningReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {LightningDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {LightningFortification}) ) 
 - For example, if lightning damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
 TotalLightningReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.35) ) = 51.25% 
 - Against other players, the total reduction would be 32.5%:
 TotalLightningReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.10) ) = 32.5%

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as lightning damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple lightning negation sources.
- Lightning Fortification is a moderately effective defensive spell with low casting requirements, usable by most starting Origins when equipped with the Two Fingers Heirloom and a Finger Seal.
- This incantation is especially valuable against Leyndell Knights, Silver Tears, and Spark Orbs, particularly in Crumbling Farum Azula, where lightning damage is prevalent.
- Lightning Fortification offers greater lightning protection than Lightningproof Dried Liver (35% vs. 15%) but at a shorter duration (90 vs. 120 seconds). This spell requires 10 Faith and 1 Memory Slot to be equipped and 20 FP to cast, while the Dried Liver only requires crafting materials.
 - The Lightningproof Dried Liver is preferable for PvP encounters, as both effects are reduced to 10%.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:

Charging the incantation increases the Attack Power to 293% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:

- Deals 5 Stance damage. Charging the spell increases the Stance damage to 9.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
 - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 25%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 44%.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- Charging this incantation more than doubles the casting time. In fact, though Knight's Lightning Spear is a good bit slower when both are cast uncharged, if they are charged they take the same amount of time to cast.
- Non-player characters will not actively try to dodge the uncharged version of this incantation. This is especially useful when fighting against evasive foes such as Tarnished-type enemies, since they are otherwise near-perfect at dodging projectile attacks.
- If the incantation hits a watery surface or an enemy standing on such a surface, a small area of effect attack with Lightning Attack Power equal to 50% of Incantation Scaling will be created that can hit the target foes and any adjacent enemies.
 - Also deals 2 Stance damage regardless of if the original Lightning Spear was charged or not.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: Grants a Body Buff that decreases holy damage taken by 60% (20% in PvP) for 70 seconds for the caster and allies within a 6-meter radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 30 FP per cast.
- Costs 20 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- This spell reduces holy damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total holy damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where *Lord'sDivineFortification* represents the effect magnitude:
 TotalHolyReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {HolyDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {Lord'sDivineFortification}) ) 
 - For example, if holy damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
 TotalHolyReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.60) ) = 51.25% 
 - Against other players, the total reduction would be 40%:
 TotalHolyReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.20) ) = 40% 
- Since it's effectively the damage taken that is reduced, the higher holy damage negation stat a character has before casting the spell, the less effective it may appear in the statistics.

sections.heading: Strategies

- The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as holy damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple holy negation sources.
- Lord's Divine Fortification is a very strong defensive spell that can significantly protect against the ranged attacks of many of the more difficult bosses, such as Maliketh, the Black Blade; Radahn, Consort of Miquella; and Radagon of the Golden Order.
- This incantation is valuable due to the prevalence of Holy damage in the game, particularly when facing enemies like Cleanrot Knights, Erdtree Avatars, Miranda Blossoms, and Oracle Envoys, especially while exploring Miquella's Haligtree.
- Lord's Divine Fortification offers greater holy protection than Divine Fortification (60% vs. 35%) but with a shorter duration (70 vs. 90 seconds). This spell requires 27 Faith, 1 Memory Slot, and 30 FP to cast, while Divine Fortification requires only 10 Faith and 20 FP.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Liurnia of the Lakes**, also known as **Liurnia**, is a region in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Liurnia is the westernmost region of the Lands Between. Characterized by its vast forests, sheer cliffs, and ever-present fog, the majority of the region is sinking into a lake. On the eastern side, the Bellum Highway runs north to south, connecting the area to the regions of Altus Plateau and Limgrave. The western coast is closely associated with the Carian royal family, and this is where their Manor stands. The Academy of Raya Lucaria rises above the lake in the center of the region, at a junction between two highroads, with the Academy Gate Town spreading around it, slowly disappearing into the waters.

The Moonlight Altar, a high plateau at the southern point, obscures the Village of the Albinaurics and its surrounding poisonous lake on the overworld map. It can only be accessed via an elevator located past the Grand Cloister deep underground, guarded by Astel, Naturalborn of the Void.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Leyndell, Royal Capital** is a legacy dungeon on the Altus Plateau in Elden Ring. This area is revealed on the map by collecting Map: Leyndell, Royal Capital.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Leyndell, Royal Capital sits at the foot of the Erdtree on Altus Plateau. It is connected to the Capital Outskirts, Forbidden Lands, and Subterranean Shunning-Grounds. The city is enclosed by double ramparts, with the city proper contained within the inner wall. The current lord of Leyndell is Morgott the Grace-Given, a Demigod of the Golden Lineage, who took it upon himself to become the Erdtree's protector, despite being born a graceless Omen.

Long ago, the city was assaulted by the colossal Ancient Dragon Gransax- the only time in recorded history that Leyndell's walls have fallen. This marked the dawn of the War of the Ancient Dragons. The bloody conflict came to an end when Godwyn the Golden befriended the dread Fortissax, an event which gave rise to the capital's Ancient Dragon Cult. Gransax's corpse can still be found towering over much of the city.

The Fortified Manor, in the southwestern portion of the city, is a perfect likeness of the Roundtable Hold. In its heyday, the manor was the headquarters of the Two Fingers and the warriors of Elden Lord Godfrey. Unlike the Table of Lost Grace, where Tarnished champions gather, the Fortified Manor is completely abandoned.

Far below the city is the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, a network of sewers and waterways inhabited by the Omen. The Leyndell Catacombs also branch off from this underground realm. Even further below lies the Cathedral of the Forsaken, where the Great Caravan of nomadic merchants were entombed so as to bury the Madness that followed them. In their underground prison they chanted a curse of despair, summoning the Frenzied Flame.

The Elden Throne sits beneath the Erdtree, in the south-eastern area of the city. It is here that Morgott stands guard, determined to protect the Erdtree from would-be champions.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Lightseeker Hyetta**, later known as **Finger Maiden Hyetta**, is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Hyetta is a blind woman who travels the Lands Between in pursuit of a distant light that she believes to lead her to her duty as a Finger Maiden. To this end, she begs for donations of Shabriri Grapes, which allow her to see the distant light in the back of her eyes. Hyetta requests grapes from The Tarnished at various points across Liurnia of the Lakes, eventually learning that the grapes she has been eating are human eyeballs, vomiting in repulsion. However, her resolve returns, and she becomes more determined than ever to become a Finger Maiden, realizing that with everyone's eyes together, the distant light is clearer. With the light seeming closer than ever, Hyetta asks the Tarnished for a Fingerprint Grape, the eye of one who has been clasped by the burned Fingers. The Tarnished fights and defeats Festering Fingerprint Vyke, a Tarnished who was scorched by the Flame of Frenzy, and offers his eyeball to Hyetta, who eats it.

If her questline has been advanced, the light guides Hyetta to the Frenzied Flame Proscription, far below the capital, where it is revealed that all along she had been guided by Three Fingers. She waits patiently on the side of the hall opposite the Site of Grace, urging the Tarnished to seek an audience with the Three Fingers, whose sanctum lies beyond a large stone door that was partially melted by searing fingerprints. Should the Tarnished allow themselves to be burned by the Flame of Frenzy and touch Hyetta's forehead, she becomes a Finger Maiden and relay the words of the Three Fingers. She reveals that all that there is came from the One Great, and that every sin and every curse was born of a mistake of the Greater Will. She states the purpose of the Flame of Frenzy: to melt everything away until all is One again. Her body then becomes engulfed in Frenzied Flames, and she burns away, leaving behind the Frenzied Flame Seal.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
For Lightseeker Hyetta to appear, you must have completed Irina of Morne's questline, meaning Irina must be dead.

1. Lake-Facing Cliffs (Liurnia of the Lakes)
 - Hyetta first appears near the Lake-Facing Cliffs Site of Grace in Liurnia of the Lakes. Exhaust her dialogue, and she shall request a Shabriri Grape.
 - Give her a Shabriri Grape, the nearest of which is south of Hyetta, found within the rear entrance to Stormveil Castle. However, the door is locked from the other side, accessible from the Stormveil Castle throne room.
1. Purified Ruins (Liurnia of the Lakes)
 - Hyetta moves to a spot close to the Purified Ruins. She again asks for a Shabriri Grape, the closest of which is east of Hyetta's location, within the Purified Ruins. It is in a secret cellar, hidden beneath some wooden planks.
 - Give her the Shabriri Grape and exhaust her dialogue.
1. Gate Town Bridge (Liurnia of the Lakes)
 - Hyetta will now appear just north of the Gate Town Bridge site of grace. She will ask for yet another Shabriri Grape. The final grape is dropped by Edgar the Revenger, who ambushes the player at the Revenger's Shack, found north of the Minor Erdtree in western Liurnia.
 - After giving her the third grape, you will have the option to tell her that the grapes are human eyes. After hearing her dialogue following this revelation, reload the area and speak to her again in the same spot.
1. Bellum Church (Bellum Highway)
 - Hyetta is next found within the ruined Bellum Church, found along the Bellum Highway. After talking to her, she will ask you to bring her a special Fingerprint Grape. This item can be obtained by defeating Festering Fingerprint Vyke, who invades the player at the Church of Inhibition in eastern Liurnia.
 - Bring Hyetta the grape and exhaust her dialogue.
1. Frenzied Flame Proscription (Subterranean Shunning-Grounds)
 - Hyetta's final location is in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, deep below Leyndell, Royal Capital, at the bottom of the Frenzied Flame Proscription. A seal at the Cathedral of the Forsaken restricts access to this location, available only after defeating Morgott, the Omen King. Exhaust her dialogue until she instructs you to unequip all Armor and interact with the burnt door at the end of the hall, past where she stands.
 - Remove all Armor and interact with the door to initiate a cutscene wherein the player meets the Three Fingers and inherits the Flame of Frenzy. (**WARNING**: this action permanently removes Melina as a companion and sets you on the path to the "Lord of the Frenzied Flame" ending, the latter of which can only be undone by using Miquella's Needle at the storm beyond time to cheat fate.)
 - After the cutscene, return to Hyetta and exhaust her dialogue. After speaking to her twice, the Frenzied Flame burns her away, leaving behind the Frenzied Flame Seal and five Frenzyflame Stones.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Hyetta will not appear if the player kills Irina of Morne early.
- Hyetta can be killed and her blood can be used to soak the Lord of Blood's Favor for White Mask Varré.
- Hyetta has the same facial appearance and voice as Irina of Morne, and she will only appear if Irina's questline has ended and she has died. Hyetta is Irina, having experienced some form of resurrection or rebirth similar to Shabriri.
- The player can meet the Three Fingers and commit the Cardinal Sin without meeting Lightseeker Hyetta, and her questline proceeds as usual if started after.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The locked, innate skill, while not unique and reliant on its weaker Intelligence-scaling, is very strong for both the projectile bullet part and the weapon stab part.
- Gains the most Attack Power (AP) from a hybrid Strength/Intelligence build (600 AP from having 45 Strength, 9 Dexterity, and 45 Intelligence), a bit less from a pure Strength build (579 AP from 80 Strength, 9 Dexterity, and 13 Intelligence), and even less from a pure Intelligence build (561 AP from 8 Strength, 12 Dexterity, and 80 Intelligence).
 - Note that since the projectile part of the skill is a bullet-type it scales with associated stat, in this case Intelligence, meaning that the pure Intelligence build will deal the most damage with that part of the skill, and that the pure Strength build will most likely end up dealing somewhat less damage overall with the skill.
- Has a unique blocking heavy attack, shared with the Carian Knight's Sword. While this can make attacking into an attacking foe a bit less punishing, the resulting Stamina damage that will be taken if hit can prevent the user from attacking or rolling away.
 - While the brief hit-stun taken by shields isn't suffered when hit, the low Stability means that using the unique heavy attack is highly likely to result in a stun from being guardbroken.
 - Stability can be increased by 10% via two-handing and then further by the Greatshield Talisman.
 - While the uncharged unique heavy attack deals the same amount of Stance damage as a normal uncharged heavy attack, but the charged version only deals 1.5 times more Stance damage, instead of the regular charged version which deals 3 times more Stance damage.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Maleigh Marais is the Lord of the Shaded Castle, a location that has been overseen by executioners for generations. He was once a private worshipper of scarlet rot, and would later become obsessed with Malenia. This is partly due to his own sickly bloodline, fueling an admiration of Malenia for remaining strong despite her own affliction.

The state of the Shaded Castle reflects this shift in fixation, as the Castellan's Hall is filled with prostheses, Cleanrot armor, and a large portrait of Malenia. This worship seems to have been blamed as part of the reason for the Shaded Castle's downfall, as Malenia is viewed as a "severed harpy" by other residents.

With the Shaded Castle sacked by Elemer of the Briar, Marais seems to have escaped as one of the few survivors, located to the west of the Castle with a Guardian Golem in his company.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Leyndell Knights** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A knight of Leyndell, distinguished by the golden canopy on their helms that marks them as one of the tree's defenders. Their armor's left breast is emblazoned with a symbol of Erdtree Worship, rumored to have been imbued with an incantation of protection. They carry with them an oval greatshield made of gold, earning the knights a reputation for their sturdiness.

All Leyndell Knights carry a Golden Greatshield. Those that wield Knight's Greatsword are capable of imbuing their armament with lightning by using Ash of War: Lightning Slash. Those that wield a Partisan are capable of calling down lightning, using Ash of War: Thunderbolt, as well as casting Rejection. They are highly skilled combatants, able to Guard Counter if an attack lands on their shields. Some Leyndell Knights wield a Greatbow, but will switch to their melee armaments upon approach. Like other knight enemies, they can also appear on horseback. There are also Frenzied Leyndell Knights on Mt. Gelmir that are capable of casting The Flame of Frenzy and Howl of Shabriri incantations.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Leyndell Foot Soldier** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: A foot soldier tasked with the protection of Leyndell. They can be found grouped together, often in the vicinity of a Leyndell Soldier or Leyndell Knight. They are nimble when wielding a Dagger or a Short Sword, but those that carry a Spear or Torchpole are less so. Some provide ranged support to their allies with a Soldier's Crossbow or by throwing Lightning Pots, whilst others employ the usage of heavier artillery such as Ballistae or Trebuchet. There are also Frenzied Leyndell Foot Soldiers on Mt. Gelmir that are capable of casting The Flame of Frenzy incantation.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Leyndell Soldiers** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A soldier sworn to defend Leyndell. They wear a surcoat bearing the majestic likeness of the Erdtree, its golden backing an honor not bestowed upon any other soldier. They fight their battles defensively and during the Shattering they were the ramparts that fortified the royal capital.

They wield either Lordsworn's Straight Sword or Warpick and can carry either a Torch or Brass Shield in their offhand. Those with a shield can perform a Guard Counter if an attack lands on their shield. They can also employ the use of a Spark Aromatic. Some of them will also carry a trumpet on their person. Upon spotting the player, they will use it and attract nearby enemies towards their position.

Some of them wield a Heavy Crossbow for ranged combat, while others are able to employ the use of Spark Aromatic. Those that wield a Partisan also carry a Lordsworn's Shield, while those that use the Lordsworn's Greatsword carry no shield but are capable of performing the Ash of War: Determination. There are also Frenzied Leyndell Soldiers on Mt. Gelmir that can cast The Flame of Frenzy incantation.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The narratives of Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign are built bit by bit and told mainly through context and environmental storytelling techniques. This page summarizes the main story and lists the major factions, characters, and events that define the Lands Between and broader *Elden Ring* setting. This page allows users to easily locate parts of the text that offer insight into each topic. Please refer to the Lore category for a complete list of articles.

sections.heading: Story
sections.markdown: In the beginning, the Greater Will fractured the One Great, which led to divisions, births, and souls. It sent its daughter, Metyr, Mother of Fingers, and its golden vassal Elden Beast through the Primeval Current to the Lands Between, the place to which all Death inevitably drifts. The Elden Beast held the power of runes and was the living embodiment of Order, and it was later forged into the great Elden Ring. The Lands Between became the arena of champions vying to become the Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Prologue
sections.markdown:
Long ago, in the Lands Between, the Two Fingers directed the Empyrean Marika to claim godhood at the Gate of Divinity and become the next vessel for the Elden Ring. Marika then waged a violent War Against the Giants to upend the Fell God and suppress the Flame of Ruin, using a Golden Seed to transform the primordial Crucible of life into the Erdtree. This act ushered in an age of Plenty. Empowered by soaring Grace of Gold, Godfrey, her first Elden Lord, and his warriors set out to conquer the entirety of the continent in her name. However, this age of abundance soon came to a swift, unforeseen end. Marika later removed the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring and commanded her loyal shadow, Maliketh, to seal it away. Thus, she, her Demigod offspring, and those blessed by her Grace of Gold would live forever, earning her the title of Queen Marika the Eternal.

Godfrey, by then known as the Lord of the Battlefield, fought until Marika's reign was absolute. When the last worthy enemy fell to his axe, the very same Grace that blessed him and his army was taken away by Marika, who instructed them to wage another war and die abroad, with the promise that life and Grace would be returned to them after death. All those who were stripped of their Grace, as well as their descendants, were Tarnished, and forced onto boats and across the Sea of Fog to carry out their Long March into the Badlands, though one vessel failed to leave. Queen Marika also sent her son Messmer and an army of outcasts on a crusade to destroy the hornsent, the old folk who dwelled in the Land of the Tower. She trapped them in the Realm of Shadow to protect herself from the Base Serpent and to conceal her shrouded origins. She later claimed Radagon of the Golden Order as her second Elden Lord, who was, in truth, her other self and a very part of her being.

After a time, Marika later instructed her children to rise as Lords or gods, or become sacrifices. She then shattered the Elden Ring, fracturing her Golden Order and releasing its Great Runes into the Lands for her children to claim. After that, Queen Marika was nowhere to be found—punished by the Elden Beast and imprisoned within the Erdtree. The Demigods were each corrupted by the power of their Great Runes, triggering the appalling Shattering, a war from which no victor arose, leading to their abandonment by the Greater Will. True to Marika's promise, it was then that the Grace of Gold returned to the Tarnished, and beckoning them back to the Lands Between so that one might repair the shattered Elden Ring and become the Elden Lord.

sections.heading: *Nightreign*
sections.markdown: Elden Ring Nightreign shares the same world and backstory as *Elden Ring*, but takes place on a parallel timeline that diverged after Marika shattered the Elden Ring. A Shattering War also took place between the Demigods; however, it had a different outcome: Heolstor the Nightlord, empowered by the Primordial Nightlord's Rune, ushered in the Night. An azure Night's Tide created the Nightlords and threatened to wash away the Lands Between. The Dreglord, a comparable threat, emerged soon after, driven by vengeance to smash the Night.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Latenna the Albinauric** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Latenna is an Albinauric woman and a deft archer. She and her wolf companion, Lobo, began their journey in the lands of the Haligtree, a sanctuary for Albinaurics. She journeyed to the far south, eventually coming to Liurnia of the Lakes.

Here, Latenna was accosted by the servants of Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing, a Tarnished wishing to gain access to the hidden lands of the Haligtree. Believing Latenna had a secret medallion that opened the way to the Haligtree, Ofnir's servants attacked her and killed her wolf, leaving her crippled, but Latenna still refused to divulge the location of the medallion, feigning ignorance.

After the Tarnished receives a half of the secret medallion from the elderly Albinauric Albus, Latenna tells them the location of the other half, and asks them to bring her along to the lands of the Haligtree, where she might fulfill her duty. The Tarnished agrees, and Latenna voluntarily becomes Spirit Ash, so they might carry her with them.

In the Mountaintops of the Giants, Latenna alerts the Tarnished that the medallion is near when they approach Castle Sol. With the second half retrieved, the path to the Haligtree is opened. She urges them to bring her to the liturgical town of Ordina. Here, a towering young Albinauric known as Phillia slumbers. Latenna grants her the birthing droplet, allowing her to create new life for all the Albinaurics. She thanks the Tarnished for their aid, promising to fight alongside them until the bitter end, requesting that they lay her to rest by Lobo once the fighting is done.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Man-Bats**, also known as **Giant Bats**, are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Man-Bats are nocturnal predators found across the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow. They commonly dwell near ancient black stone ruins but also populate caves, mines, and forts. By day, they often sit idly or hang from ruins; by night, they become far more active and aggressive. Man-Bats are frequently encountered in groups alongside matriarchal Operatic Bats, whose mournful Latin arias blame Marika for their vile circumstances.

Dark, leathery skin wraps these emaciated winged creatures, from whose backs sprout tufts of silvery hair. Their enormous ears aid in echolocation, and the undersides of their membraned wings bear a layer of striking patterned fur. While Man-Bats may crawl around using their forelimbs, they prefer to fly during combat. They attack using their sharp hind claws and, if they get close enough, by sinking long, dagger-like fangs into their prey. They are capable of emitting a concussive sonar screech that can strike from range.

Two distinct varieties of Man-Bat exist, each identified by the color and pattern of fur growing on the front of their wing. The common Man-Bat is distinguished by vivid bright red fur with yellow markings. The Elite variant, exclusive to the Mountaintops of the Giants, has duller wings that fiercely display eyespot mimicry. Additionally, it possesses significantly greater HP, and yield more runes upon defeat.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- In the , Man-Bats possessed a cut animation in which they stood upright and sang "Herutun Rutun" by Umeko Ando a cappella. The song is performed in Ainu, a critically endangered language indigenous to Japan.
 - , an oral storytelling tradition practiced by the Ainu, is told in first-person and often describes the world from the perspectives of animals.
 - This animation may have been a placeholder for the "Song of Lament" sung by Operatic Bats.

sections.markdown: Living Jars** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Sentient, animated jars found throughout the Lands Between. They are brought to life by human flesh and blood, and are considered a kindly folk, however they will protect themselves from perceived threats. They contain human innards within them, from which they inherit the dregs of those who came before. Fragments of their bodies are sought after due to the magical power locked within, making them targets of poachers.

An enclave of peaceful Living Jars reside in Jarburg, on the cliffs of Liurnia of the Lakes.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Small, childlike Living Jars, often found under the protection of Warrior Jars. They are often passive unless provoked.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Living Jars with distinct yellow lids. Their primary tactic is to rush at their enemies and then explode, killing themselves and dealing damage to friends and foes alike. They will also explode if they come into contact with fire.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Larger Living Jars that contain the remnants of warriors. They pass these warrior's innards from jar to jar, carrying their dreams of greatness with them.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The Companion Jar talisman mentions that perhaps they were made to be better than their innards. In Shadow of the Erdtree, it is revealed that undesirable people were stuffed into jars so that they could be reborn into good people. Shamans then perform their worship at gaols where they offer their prayers to the innards of the greatjars, such that they might be reborn one day into sainthood, or good people. This is the cycle of death and rebirth, taken into the hands of mortal men.
 - Living Jars drop Raw Meat Dumplings that contain teeth and inflict Poison, not unlike the Poison-inflicting Tooth Whips used by Greater Potentates to tenderize Shamans.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- In the context of Living Jars, "saint" and "sainthood" refer to "a very virtuous, kind, or patient person" and "a person acknowledged as holy or virtuous and typically regarded as being in heaven after death." The Japanese version uses 善き人 (lit. "good/righteous person"), rather than terms specific to Catholic and Orthodox saints. This applies to the following texts:
 - "*I swear**—a living saint** I'll surely be!*" Stranded Souls -> 天に誓う。**善き人**になる
 - "***Nigh-sainthood** itself awaits you within.*" Stranded Souls -> そして、**善き人**になりなさい
 - "*This is what becomes of the condemned, who get sliced up and stuffed into jars to become **saints** instead.*" Innard Meat -> **善き人**になるために 切り刻まれ、大壺に詰め込まれた罪人どもの なれの果てである
 - "*They offer their prayers to the innards of the greatjars, such that they might be reborn one day into **sainthood.***" Greatjar -> その祈りは大壺の中身に捧げられる いつか、**善き人**として生まれ変わるように それは、人の手による輪廻である

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Land Squirts** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Land Squirts are stationary creatures that release poisonous gas when threatened. Their fleshy, tube-like bodies remain rooted in place, continuously spraying poison into their surroundings when approached.

Land Squirts are vulnerable on their soft undersides and to their own element. Inflicting Poisoned status on a poison Land Squirt will cause it to explode, potentially creating a chain reaction among nearby Land Squirts.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Land Squirts can be staggered and riposted.
- They fall over when staggered, exposing their soft underbellies.
- When poisoned, they explode, creating a chain reaction among nearby Land Squirts.
- Found primarily near water sources.
- The spirit of three Land Squirts can be summoned using Land Squirt Ashes.
